description:
## Goal

A reached protocol callback call whose receiver cannot match any known or demandable implementation must fail compilation with a stable source diagnostic. It must never survive semantic closure as an unresolved call edge or panic during artifact materialization.

This is direct protocol dispatch, distinct from:

- fz-kdt.2: `Protocol.t(...)` contract obligations.
- fz-kdt.11: missing builtin impl-target families such as `Tuple`.

## Current state

Pinned clean `origin/main`: `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`.

Fixture:

```fz
defprotocol P do
  fn each(value)
end

defimpl P, for: List do
  fn each(value), do: value
end

fn main(), do: P.each(42)
```

`P.each/1` is reached with receiver type `int`; the only known provider target is `List`.

`resolve_protocol_call` in `src/compiler2/jobs/semantic.rs:1411-1434` reads `ProtocolImplProviders`, demands any overlapping unloaded providers, but then returns `CallSiteResolution::Unresolved` even when there are no overlapping providers and therefore nothing left to wait for.

That unresolved value is published as a settled `CallSiteSummary` fact. This is proved by the passing test `a_reached_callsite_that_names_no_target_publishes_an_unresolved_edge`.

Artifact production waits only for the settled fact (`jobs/artifact.rs:75-84`). `World::callsite_summary` exposes only a resolved summary, so `materialize_direct_call_edge` receives `None`, `materialize_call_edges` returns `None`, and `jobs/artifact.rs:155` panics:

```text
product materialization should have complete call edges after waits
```

Fresh production-door results from the pinned worktree:

```text
fz2 interp fixtures2/00424_protocol_no_impl.fz -> exit 101, panic at artifact.rs:155
fz2 run fixtures2/00424_protocol_no_impl.fz    -> exit 101, same panic
fz2 build fixtures2/00424_protocol_no_impl.fz
  -o /tmp/fz-kdt149-built                      -> exit 101, same panic; no output
```

The nominal regression `protocol_call_on_non_implementing_type_emits_diagnostic` is false-green: it only calls `compiler.drive()`, makes no assertion, and leaves the desired diagnostic as a TODO.

## Strategy

Use the output-contract loop:

1. Replace the false-green fixture test with a red assertion for the complete diagnostic.
2. Give protocol resolution a terminal "no applicable implementation" outcome distinct from transient `Unresolved`, a provider boundary, and a dead callsite.
3. Emit that error while protocol/provider facts and receiver evidence are still available; do not patch artifact materialization to silently drop the call.
4. Propagate the same fatal diagnostic through interp, JIT, and AOT preparation.
5. Update protocol documentation with the settled no-match rule.

## Signal

Add stable `type/protocol-no-impl` diagnostic coverage for fixture 00424, including its callsite span and semantic names/types. Exercise all three CLI doors and retain fixture 00425 as the positive matching-implementation control.

## Acceptance

- Fixture 00424 emits one fatal `type/protocol-no-impl` diagnostic naming protocol/callback `P.each/1`, receiver type `int`, known implementation target `List`, and the `P.each(42)` source span.
- `interp`, `run`, and `build` all exit nonzero with the same diagnostic contract. None prints `panicked`, the artifact invariant text, or a Rust backtrace.
- `build` creates no output executable after the diagnostic.
- The existing false-green planner test is replaced with assertions over the diagnostic; no TODO-only test remains for 00424.
- Semantic tests distinguish transient unresolved while a relevant provider can still land, terminal no-applicable-implementation after protocol dispatch/provider facts settle, and resolved provider-boundary/dead-callsite states.
- `00425_protocol_impl_match.fz` remains resolved and executable.
- Protocol docs describe the terminal no-match behavior.
- Full library, CLI, and fixture-matrix suites pass.
title: Diagnose a protocol call when its receiver has no implementation
